Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CH1400 : Environment and Safety Engineering { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Coordinator :

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Environmental Engineering: Introduction to Environmental Engineering Nature and scope of environment problems Ecosystem Local, regional and global environmental challenges, Basic concepts of biodiversity and its significance.
Water Pollution
Fundamentals and Control Strategies: Water quality-physical, chemical & biological characteristics, Drinking water standards, Effluent quality requirements, Water and wastewater treatment processes-treatment train, physical, chemical and biological unit operations
Module 2 :

Fundamentals and Control Strategies Air pollution - sources, classifications and regulations and their effects, Monitoring Principles and instrumentation for particulate and gaseous pollutant measurements Air pollution control strategies: physical, chemical and biological methods.

Module 3 :

Noise Pollution: Noise standards and criteria, Noise pollution measurement in ambient air and industrial complex, Control methods for noise pollution Engineering principles in waste management, Case studies on industrial applications of cleaner technologies in industries. Environment Management and Sustainability Tools for sustainable management including ISO certification, environment audit, EIA 4h

Module 4 :

Safety Engineering: Introduction: Background, Benefits of safety in Industry, Safety Terms and Definitions. Safety Mathematics and Reliability Basics: Basic Statistics, Set Algebra, Probability, Reliability.
Workplace Accidents and Safety: Accident Causation Theories (Domino Theory, Human Factor Theory), Accident Investigation and Reporting. Legal Aspects of Safety: Factories Act 1948, Other International Codes (OSHA Laws & Regulations).

Module 5 :

Hazards Related to Various Industries: Chemical, Electrical, Mining, and Construction Safety and Risk Management: Safety Management Principles, Safety Program Plan, Safety Committees, Safety Performance Measures, Risk Assessment, Risk Management. Safety Analysis Methods: FMEA, FTA, Markov Method, HAZOP, JHA,
Control Charts. Human Factors in Safety: Job Stress, Ergonomics, Human behaviour Personal Protective Equipment Safety Costing Safety Cost Estimation Methods, Safety Cost Estimation

Module 6 :

Introduction to Standardization Quality Ecosystem, Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), roles and functions of BIS. Purpose of Standardization and certification of products, process and services. Important Indian and International standards, Importance of standard for ensuring product quality, environment, safety and sustainability. Indian standards on safety and Environment.

Course Objective

1 .

Convey ideas of the interdisciplinary nature of the environment
2 .

To learn about environmental pollution controlling stratagies
3 .

Aware of the basic concepts of industrial safety engineering
4 .

Ability to assess safety in various places
5 .

Convey idea of Standardization and overview of Standards on safety and environment

Course Outcome

1 .

Know the fundamentals of ecosystem and the importance of environmental engineering

2 .

Design water treatment units and assess the water quality parameters

3 .

Evaluate the design strategies for air and noise pollution control

4 .

Understand the terminologies related to industrial safety engineering and management

5 .

Analyze the industrial safety using different analysis techniques
6 .

Identify and use Standards on Environment and Safety aspects

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CH6330 : Computational Transport Phenomena { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: Governing Equations
Laws of fluid motion and boundary conditions
Module 2: Steady diffusion Problem
Finite volume method for 1D steady state diffusion problem, Finite volume method for 2D steady state diffusion problem, Finite volume method for 3D steady state diffusion problem
Module 3: Steady state convection-diffusion problem
Finite volume method for 1D steady state convection-diffusion problem, Finite volume method for 2D steady state convection-diffusion problem, Finite volume method for 3D steady state convection-diffusion problem, Higher-order differencing schemes
Module 4: Pressure-velocity coupling in steady flow
Pressure-velocity coupling to solve steady state momentum transport problems, Application of SIMPLE, SIMPLER, SIMPLEC and PISO algorithms
Module 5: Solution of discretised equations
Solution for 1D Problem, Solution for 2D Problem
Module 6: Unsteady flow problems
Unsteady diffusion problems, Unsteady convection-diffusion problems, Solution algorithm for unsteady flow problems
Module 7: Boundary conditions
Implementation of boundary conditions

Course Objective

1 .

To provide an introduction to the scientific principles and practical engineering applications of computational fluid dynamics
2 .

To teach students how to solve different momentum, mass and heat transfer problems
3 .

To teach student how to develop in-house code to simulate the diffusive and convective-diffusive problems

Course Outcome

1 .

Doing this course student will be able
CO1: to discretize the momentum, mass and energy transport equations by finite volume technique
CO2: to apply different CFD algorithms to solve different level transport phenomena problems
CO3: to understand the transport phenomena problems better by analysing CFD results
CO4: to develop in-house CFD computer code

Essential Reading

1 .

H. K. Versteeg and W. Malalasekera, An Introduction to Computational Fluid Dynamics: The Finite Volume Method, Longman Scientific & Technical , 2nd Ed, 2007

2 .

3. K. Muralidhar, and T. Sundararajan, Computational Fluid Flow and Heat Transfer, Narosa Publishing House , 1995

Supplementary Reading

1 .

V. Patankar, Numerical Heat Transfer and Fluid Flow, Taylor and Francis , 1978

2 .

S K. Gupta, Numerical Methods for Engineers, New Age Publishers , 1995

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CS3009 : Operating Systems { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Introduction to operating systems: review of computer organization, operating system structures, system calls, system programs, virtual machine, Process concept, Process scheduling, Operations on processes, Cooperating processes, Inter-Process-Communication (IPC), Communication in client-server systems
CPU Scheduling: Scheduling criteria, Scheduling algorithms, Multiple processor scheduling, Real time scheduling, Algorithm evaluation
Process synchronization: The critical section problem, Synchronization hardware, Semaphores, Classical problems of synchronization
Deadlock: Methods for handling deadlocks, Deadlock Prevention, Deadlock Avoidance, Deadlock Detection, Recovery from Deadlock
Memory Management: Background, Swapping, Contiguous memory allocation, Paging, Segmentation, Segmentation with paging, Virtual memory - Background, Demand Paging, Process Creation, Page replacement, Allocation of frames, Thrashing
File System Interface: File Concept, Access methods, Directory Structure, Allocation methods, Free space management, Disk Scheduling, Disk Management

Course Objective

1 .

General understanding of structure of modern computers
2 .

To understand the purpose, structure and functions of operating systems
3 .

Understanding Processes, Interprocess communication, process scheduling and process synchronization
4 .

Understanding the principles main memory and secondary memory management

Course Outcome

1 .

At the end of the course, students shall be equipped with the knowledge to:
CO1: identify the problems related to process management and synchronization and apply learned methods to solve basic problems.
CO2: comprehend the cause and effect related to deadlocks and to analyse them related to common circumstances in operating systems.
CO3: perceive the use of virtual memory in modern operating systems and the structure of the most common file-systems.

Essential Reading

1 .

Abraham Silberschatz, Peter B. Galvin, Greg Gagne, Operating System Concepts, Wiley

2 .

William Stallings, Operating Systems, Internals and Design Principles, Pearson Education

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Andrew S. Tanenbaum, Herbert Bos, Modern Operating Systems, Prentice Hall

2 .

Remzi Arpaci-Dusseau, Andrea Arpaci-Dusseau, Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces, Arpaci-Dusseau Books

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : MN2004 : Mine Surveying { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: Introduction to Mine Survey [2 Hours]
Definition of survey, importance of survey in mine, types of survey.
Module 2: Chain Survey [4 Hours]
Distance measurement using chain/tape, Ranging & chaining of survey lines, surveying in obstacles in chaining, Field work & Plotting of maps using chain survey.
Module 3: Compass survey [4 Hours]
Types of compass, use of compass, bearing of a line, dial traverse and adjustments, local attractions and correction of bearings.
Module 4: Theodolite survey [4 Hours]
Types of theodolite: seconds theodolites, micro-optic theodolites, electronic theodolites, measurement of horizontal angles and vertical angles using theodolite Traversing – surface and underground including boundary surveys and joint surveys, survey errors and their adjustments, co-ordinate calculations.
Module 5: Levelling [4 Hours]
Types of levels, setting of level instruments and levelling staff, types of levelling methods- reciprocal levelling, profile levelling, differential levelling, reduction of levels by height of instrument method and rise and fall method, Concept of contour, Methods of contouring and uses of contours.
Module 6: Tacheometry surveying [3 Hours]
Methods of tacheometry survey. Field work and computation
Module 7: Correlation Survey [3 Hours]
Correlation of surface and underground surveys: Verticality of shafts, shaft depth measurement, Direct traversing in inclined shaft, correlation in vertical shaft –single and two shafts .
Module 8: Setting out curves – surface and underground. [3 Hours]
Module 9: Computation of areas and volumes [3 Hours]
Module 10: Special Mine Surveys [3 Hours]
Triangulation: Classification of Triangulation systems, Triangulation figures, Base line measurements Surveys for connecting national grid, survey of installations of mine structures, EDM and its application, surveying by Modern instruments by using GPS & Total Station.
GIS and Remote Sensing Applications in mine map preparation.

Course Objective

1 .

Make understanding the role of Mine survey course in mine operations
2 .

Enable to learn the method of conducting the mine survey
3 .

Enable to prepare and understand the mine maps

Course Outcome

1 .

CO1: Develop necessary analytical skills, methods and ways of conducting mine survey.
CO2: Students will able to learn the tools needed to conduct mine survey
CO3: Solve the mine survey related problems.
CO4: Preparing and understanding the mine survey plans

Subject {L-T-P / C} : PH4073 : Computer Programming Laboratory { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: (6 hours)
Setting up Python environment and learn how to use it. Handling strings, input() and print() statements. Variables, assignment, and string concatenation. Introduction to List methods, List slicing, and IF/ELSE constructs.
Module 2: (6 hours)
Introduction to FOR loop. FOR loop with IF/ELSE statement. Handling integer, floats, and introduction to arithmetic operations. Introduction to the Python module RANDOM, finding the probability distribution of the outcomes of throwing two or more dice.
Module 3 (6 hours)
The WHILE loop and the logical operators AND, OR, NOT, NOT IN. Introduction to the data type Boolean. Lists and arithmetic operations, nested FOR loops, list FLATTENING.
Module 4: (9 hours)
Introduction to the data type DICTIONARY and list of dictionaries. Application of dictionaries. User defined FUNCTION and DATABASE creation.
Module 5: (9 hours)
Working with files: reading from a file, working with a file’s contents, writing to a file , storing data. Creating and using a CLASS.

Course Objective

1 .

To familiarize students with the Python programming, including variables, strings, lists, and control flow structures.
2 .

To develop problem-solving skills using loops (FOR and WHILE) and logical operators.
3 .

To introduce fundamental data structures like lists and dictionaries, and their practical applications in data handling and storage.
4 .

To provide hands-on experience with object-oriented programming concepts, file handling, and database creation in Python.

Course Outcome

1 .

At the end of the course, students will be able to:
CO1: Set up a Python environment and effectively use basic programming constructs.
CO2: Demonstrate proficiency in using loops (FOR, WHILE) and conditional statements.
CO3: Implement Python's built-in data structures and apply them in real-world scenarios.
CO4: Gain the ability to design user-defined functions, create and use classes, and manage file operations.

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : PA5961 : Internship { 0-0-0 / 11}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module I
Performance evaluation by the Training agency: The student shall undertake Professional Training for a period of at least 20 weeks with a training agency approved by the Departmental Training & Placement In-Charge. A Training Manual shall be provided to the training agency containing details of the expected outline of work and other procedures. The student’s overall performance during the tenure of the internship would be graded by the competent authority at the training agency based on the following performance criteria as outlined in the Training Manual.
1) Design Acumen: Ideation, conceptualization, analyses of issues, innovation in solutions, and development of designs.
2) Drafting and Presentation: Development of various types of drawings, simulations, graphics, reports, or slide presentations.
3) Site Supervision: Understanding the requirements at the site and formulating necessary response/action.
4) Work Ethics: Punctuality in reporting, meeting assigned deadlines, putting in extra effort when required, enthusiasm and self-motivation in getting involved and taking responsibilities.
5) Social Skills: Maintaining the expected professional appearance, ability to harmoniously work with a team, amicable professional interactions, and communication skills.
Module II
Performance evaluation by the Institute: The following tasks, undertaken by the student during the training period, to be assessed by the institute.
1) Preparation of sketch designs, presentation drawings, etc. Municipal drawings according to the byelaws Working drawings and details Estimates, bill of quantities, and specifications
2) Discussions with clients structural consultants services consultants
3) Inspection and management of site – preparation of models, perspective views, and photographs reports, progress charts, etc.
4) Other administrative works. Assignment: After the completion of training, students shall submit a report containing the profile of the training agency and project-wise details of work undertaken by the student. All projects listed in the report shall correspond with the list of projects mentioned in the monthly log. Copies of drawings prepared by the student at the training agency shall be obtained with due permission of the agency and stamped and signed by the competent authority at the agency. The same shall be provided as an annexure.

Course Objective

1 .

To gain comprehensive knowledge of architectural practice and its day-to-day requirements from hands-on experience as an intern.
2 .

To develop skill competencies as an architect.

Course Outcome

1 .

1. Ability to develop skills and professional ethics in architectural practice.
2. Ability to communicate design ideas with varied stakeholders and coordinate on-site design implementation.
3. Ability to work in a team to perform various tasks related to an architectural project.

Essential Reading

1 .

Srivastava, A. & Radford, A., The elements of modern architecture: Understanding contemporary buildings, Tames & Hudson, London

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : PH5138 : Materials Physics and Engineering { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

(8 hrs) Foundations of Materials Physics: metals, insulators, semiconductors, superconductors, topological materials, Overview of atomic bonding: quantum mechanical origin, Relationship between material properties and quantum states. Crystallography and Quantum Mechanics of Solids: Bravais lattices and reciprocal space, Electron states in periodic potentials (Bloch’s theorem), Nearly free electron model vs. tight-binding model. Electronic Band Structure and Fermi Surfaces: Kronig-Penney model and energy gaps, Effective mass and electron/hole transport, Density of states and Fermi surfaces.

Module 2 :

(6 hrs) Lattice Vibrations and thermal properties: phonons and lattice dynamics, quantum description of lattice vibrations, phonon dispersion relations, specific heat of solids: Einstein vs. Debye models. Thermal conductivity and phonon scattering, Wiedemann-Franz law and electronic transport, Electron-phonon interactions.
Module 3 :

(8 hrs) Advanced Electronic Materials: semiconductor physics and applications, intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors, p-n junctions and carrier dynamics, quantum Hall effect and topological states. Magnetism and Magnetic Materials: quantum origins of magnetism, exchange interactions and spin waves, ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, and spintronics. Dielectric and Ferroelectric Materials: polarization mechanisms and electric susceptibility, ferroelectricity and phase transitions.
Module 4 :

(8 hrs) Quantum and Correlated Materials: Type I vs. Type II superconductors, High-temperature superconductors, Cooper pairs and BCS theory. Strongly Correlated Electron Systems: Mott insulators and Hubbard models, quantum phase transitions. Topological Materials.
Module 5 :

(6 hrs) Materials for Quantum Technologies: 2D materials, graphene and transition metal dichalcogenides, Quantum dots and photonic materials, Materials for superconducting qubits. Experimental Probes of Materials: X-ray diffraction (XRD) and neutron scattering, Scanning probe techniques: AFM and STM, Electron microscopy: TEM and SEM.

Course Objective

1 .

To impart knowledge on:
Foundational understanding of the quantum mechanical basis of material properties, including electronic structure, bonding, and lattice dynamics,

2 .

Key models of electrons and phonons in solids, emphasizing how microscopic behavior governs macroscopic physical properties like conductivity and magnetism,
3 .

Advanced material classes, including semiconductors, magnetic materials, ferroelectrics, superconductors, and topological phases,
4 .

Quantum and correlated materials, highlighting emergent phenomena and their theoretical background,
5 .

State-of-the-art characterization techniques and materials relevant for quantum technologies.

Course Outcome

1 .

At the end of course, students will be able to:
CO1:.Understand crystal structures, bonding, and electronic band structure from first principles.
2 .

CO2: Analyze electronic band structure and the physics of semiconductors.
3 .

CO3: Describe lattice dynamics, phonons, and heat capacity using quantum theory.
4 .

CO4: Explore topological materials, superconductivity, and strongly correlated systems.
5 .

CO5: Use experimental techniques such as X-ray diffraction and electron microscopy to probe materials.

Essential Reading

1 .

C. Kittel, Introduction to Solid State Physics, Wiley India Edition (2019).

2 .

Ashcroft & Mermin, Solid State Physics, Brooks/Cole; New edition (2021).

3 .

S. M. Girvin & K. Yang, Modern Condensed Matter Physics, Cambridge University Press, (2019).

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Jeno Sólyom, Fundamentals of the Physics of Solids Vol I, II, III, Springer 2009.

2 .

Callister & Rethwisch, Materials Science and Engineering: An Introduction, Wiley; 9th edition (2013).
